rationale: RUST-D31: pins the `imports` relationship this lane never emitted. One row per SCOPE, because the source is the fact under test: a file-top-level `use` is named by the file's own rust module name (`use-import-edges` for this file, by rust's own rule that a file's module is its stem), an inline `mod`'s `use` by that module (`inner`), and a function-local `use` by that function (`scoped`). Also pins the TARGET contract: the edge names the PATH AS WRITTEN, so a simple `use std::collections::HashMap;` targets `std::collections::HashMap` and a group `use std::io::{Read, Write as W};` targets the group's prefix `std::io` — the ImportInfo row's own spelling (RUST-D10/RUST-D29), reused rather than re-derived, because a stripped prefix would be an inference the source does not make. And the group/alias contract on the edge's `items` (`Write as W` binds `W`), the 1.0 confidence (the path is written verbatim) and the `import_based` evidence tier, which is the tier every other lane's import edge carries and which the fall-through branch stamped `usage_contextual` on before. The two forbid rows are the two defects this edge class invites: a `"global"` source (a magic name no rust source declares) and a module path with no items resolved. SUPERSESSION (2026-10-19, Lead decision §21.11 task-36 defect 3, task-9 conditions): (a) the FILE-SCOPE source is the family's declared `(file)` spelling — the M60/#910 flag the store acts on rewrites it to the project-relative path; the older expectation of the file's module NAME predates that spelled contract. (b) the edge TARGET is the MODULE the path depends on (`std::collections` for `use std::collections::HashMap`), with the bound names carried on `meta.items` — the older expectation used the full written path, which puts the BINDING into the dependency target; the module prefix is the unit the name model and the file claims price, and the group form (`std::io` + items [Read,W]) already used it. Coverage is preserved: every row still pins its scope, its bindings (alias-aware), its module target and line; the function-scope row is now real (source = the function) and `fileLevel` is never set on it. LINE PIN UPDATED (2026-10-19): the fixture header gained the supersession note above the `use` line, shifting the pinned path line; the expectation follows the source line (the pin is about which LINE the edge names, not its historic number).
